hero.subtitle: I build the engineering layer behind Unity games — editor tooling, UI infrastructure, and multiplayer systems, from VR training platforms to deterministic rollback netcode.

about.headline: I build what's
paragraphs: Professional Unity developer since 2022, building in Unity since 2017. My work spans VR training tools, AR content pipelines, multiplayer architecture, and UI infrastructure — the common thread is systems other developers build on top of: editor tools, reusable UI, and networked game state that has to stay correct under real players.

Outside client work, I build my own projects with the same discipline: Totally Witchin', a multiplayer brawler running on Photon Quantum's deterministic rollback netcode, and a reusable first-person Unity framework — architecture designed to be reused, and already reused twice.

bullets: Implemented UI features, localisation, and custom UI components across the company's product lineup
Designed and built a drag-and-drop graph editor extension for the in-house content-creator app, enabling branching-story authoring
Built foundational UI infrastructure used across the product line: BOOKR Tween (an in-house tweening system) and a shader-based corner-rounding UI primitive, both with inspector tooling
Designed and built a reusable theming system with per-product colour schemes and optional sub-modes (e.g. light/dark)
Built a custom Unity Timeline extension for animating complex parent-child hierarchies — a gap in Timeline's native capability
Built a separate TMP Text Timeline extension for text-transition handling, plus content-creator-facing editor tooling around both, cutting per-animation creation time by ~60%
Investigated migration of the company's legacy AR app (printed-book marker tracking with 3D animated overlays) to a modern AR stack and Unity Addressables-based content delivery
Built the authoring workspace and state synchronisation for Mentis.Live, a team-built browser-based editor for OSH VR training content
Retrofitted VoxSys with input abstraction, weapon handling and rig swapping, letting PC players join existing VR sessions in this team-built shooter
For an AR virtual pet game, designed and built the behaviour stack — a ScriptableObject state machine integrated with Unity's animation system, with designer-facing editor tooling
Implemented gameplay UI across projects with LeanTween-animated elements and custom-built widgets

items.title: Orbital Duel
items.description: A spaceship PvP shooter where movement is constrained to orbits — ships rotate around a gravitational centre and shift lanes inward or outward to attack.

techs.label: Unity
techs.desc: Game engine used for the entire project — rendering, physics, input, and all gameplay systems.

techs.label: C#
techs.desc: Primary language for all gameplay logic, movement systems, and game state management.

techs.label: Photon Quantum
techs.desc: Deterministic networking framework ensuring pixel-perfect, lag-free multiplayer across all clients.

techs.label: Multiplayer Architecture
techs.desc: Designed around a server-authoritative loop — all orbital positions and combat resolved deterministically.

techs.label: Retro Pixel Aesthetic
techs.desc: Custom pixel-style visuals to give the game a classic arcade feel while running on modern netcode.

items.title: Spell Brawl
items.description: A platformer brawler with a unique two-phase loop — draft spells into your spellbook during Pick phase, then unleash them in order during Fight phase.

techs.label: Unity
techs.desc: Full game engine foundation — handles 2D physics, scene management, and all rendering.

techs.label: C#
techs.desc: All gameplay systems — phase management, spellbook logic, ability sequencing, and player controllers.

techs.label: VContainer
techs.desc: Dependency injection framework — decouples systems so the Fight and Pick phases are independently testable.

techs.label: UniTask
techs.desc: Async/await framework for Unity — drives phase transitions, ability animations, and UI sequences without coroutines.

techs.label: DOTween
techs.desc: Animation library for spell effects, UI transitions, and the satisfying feel of the spellbook drafting UI.

techs.label: Multiplayer
techs.desc: Networked game loop synchronising the Pick and Fight phases across all connected players in real time.

items.title: Plush Keeper
items.description: A warm emotional simulator — run a plush shop inherited from your estranged father, build a relationship through daily shop life, and discover why the hobby matters.

techs.label: Unity
techs.desc: Engine powering the cozy shop sim — 2D scene management, save system, and all visual presentation.

techs.label: C#
techs.desc: Shop logic, inventory systems, narrative state machine, and character interaction systems.

techs.label: DOTween
techs.desc: Animates the shop's cozy feel — plush bounces, dialogue popups, and gentle UI transitions.

techs.label: Narrative Design
techs.desc: Story unfolds through shop interactions — relationship with the father deepens as the player progresses days.

techs.label: Blender
techs.desc: Used for 3D asset modelling of the plush characters and shop props that define the game's visual identity.
